inspectedText: Read pp.29–36: plan to present Ellen as an invalid white gentleman with William as attendant; male presentation relates to expected travel conventions, not a demonstrated universal law. She could not write; right-hand poultice/sling is proposed to ask others to register. Chin/cheek bandage conceals beardless chin; green spectacles obscure eyes; illness excuses conversation. pp.51–53: Charleston official initially refuses signature substitute; fellow traveler helps. pp.69–74: Baltimore officials demand security or endorsement showing supposed ownership due stated railway liability; conductor confirms prior train travel; departure bell and apparent illness precede discretionary permission. No ownership proof is actually supplied. pp.78–82: Philadelphia arrival and later reading/writing lessons. pp.87–93: Boston recapture threat and departure for England.
limitations: Exact dialogue, reconstructed emotions and surrounding anecdotes are not transcripts or adopted facts.
Weekdays conflict with 1848 calendar; use December1848, not precise daily dates.
The portrait omits facial poultice deliberately; it is a later portrait, not escape-day imagery.
